_about: Popular 'facts' that are false, each with what is actually true and where that comes from. 'patterns' are regular expressions that must all match within one sentence; 'examples' are phrasings that must be caught, and are checked by the tests. A myth is answered before any parallel, because the right reply to a myth is not an equally irrelevant number, it is no.

myths.claim: We only use 10% of our brains
myths.truth: Brain imaging shows activity across virtually every region over the course of a day. There is no idle 90%
examples: You only use 10% of your brain
humans use ten percent of their brains

myths.claim: People swallow eight spiders a year in their sleep
myths.truth: No study has ever found this. A sleeping, breathing, snoring person is a source of vibration that spiders tend to avoid
examples: The average person eats 8 spiders a year while sleeping
we swallow spiders in our sleep

myths.claim: You lose most of your body heat through your head
myths.truth: The head is about 10% of the body's surface and loses roughly that share of heat. An uncovered head is no worse than any other uncovered part
examples: we lose 50 percent of our body heat through our heads
most of your heat escapes through your head

myths.claim: You need to drink eight glasses of water a day
myths.truth: No study supports a fixed eight glasses. Water in food and other drinks counts, and for healthy people thirst is a good guide
examples: you need 8 glasses of water a day
drink eight glasses of water daily

myths.claim: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker
myths.truth: Shaving cuts hair at its widest point, so the stubble feels coarse. It does not change how thick, dark or fast hair grows
examples: shaving makes your hair grow back thicker
if you shave it grows back darker

myths.claim: Hair and nails keep growing after death
myths.truth: The skin dries and retracts after death, which makes hair and nails look longer. Growth needs a working body
examples: your hair and nails keep growing after death
fingernails grow after you die

myths.claim: Reading in dim light ruins your eyesight
myths.truth: It can cause temporary eye strain, but there is no evidence it does lasting damage
examples: reading in dim light ruins your eyesight
reading in low light damages your eyes

myths.claim: Turkey makes you sleepy
myths.truth: Turkey has no more tryptophan than chicken or beef. A very large meal, and often alcohol, is the more likely culprit
examples: turkey makes you sleepy because of the tryptophan
eating turkey makes you tired

myths.claim: Sugar makes children hyperactive
myths.truth: A meta-analysis of double-blind trials found no effect of sugar on children's behaviour or thinking
examples: sugar makes kids hyperactive
the kids are hyper from all that sugar

myths.claim: Swallowed gum stays in your stomach for seven years
myths.truth: Gum base is not digested, but it passes through the gut like anything else, in days
examples: swallowed gum takes 7 years to digest
gum stays in your stomach for seven years

myths.claim: One dog year is seven human years
myths.truth: Dogs age fastest early on: a one-year-old dog is closer to a human of 30. The seven-to-one rule fits no age
examples: one dog year is 7 human years
dogs age seven years for every one of ours

myths.claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from space
myths.truth: It is long but narrow, and roughly the colour of the land around it. Astronauts, including China's first, report they could not see it with the naked eye
examples: the Great Wall of China is the only man-made thing visible from space
you can see the great wall from the moon

myths.claim: Cracking your knuckles gives you arthritis
myths.truth: Studies comparing habitual knuckle-crackers with everyone else find no difference in arthritis
myths.source: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine
examples: cracking your knuckles gives you arthritis
stop cracking your knuckles, you'll get arthritis

myths.claim: Lightning never strikes the same place twice
myths.truth: It often does, especially tall, pointed and isolated things. The Empire State Building is struck around 20 times a year
examples: lightning never strikes the same place twice
lightning doesn't strike twice

myths.claim: Blood is blue until it meets oxygen
myths.truth: Blood is always red, darker when it carries less oxygen. Veins look blue because of how skin absorbs and scatters light
examples: blood is blue until it hits the air
your blood is actually blue inside your veins

myths.claim: Food dropped for under five seconds is safe to eat
myths.truth: Bacteria can transfer from a surface to food in under a second. Wet food on a dirty surface picks up the most
examples: the five second rule
it's fine, 5 second rule

myths.claim: Goldfish have a three-second memory
myths.truth: Goldfish can be trained to respond to sounds, colours and feeding times, and remember them for months
examples: goldfish have a 3 second memory
memory like a goldfish, three seconds

myths.claim: Vaccines cause autism
myths.truth: The 1998 paper behind this was retracted. A study of 657,461 Danish children found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism
examples: vaccines cause autism
the MMR jab is linked to autism

myths.claim: Bats are blind
myths.truth: No bat species is blind. Many see well, and some fruit bats rely on sight more than echolocation
examples: bats are blind
blind as a bat, literally

myths.claim: Napoleon was unusually short
myths.truth: He was about 1.69 m (5 ft 7 in), average or a little above for a Frenchman of his day. French inches were longer than English ones, which started the story
examples: Napoleon was really short
he's got a Napoleon complex, you know Napoleon was tiny

myths.claim: Vikings wore horned helmets
myths.truth: No horned helmet has ever been found from the Viking Age. The image comes from 19th-century costume design for Wagner's operas
examples: Vikings wore horned helmets
a viking helmet with horns
